en: To lean back comfortably in a seat; or to relax; or to watch without getting involved.
ex: Just sit back and enjoy the show.
坐下來好好欣賞表演吧。

en: To manage without something or someone that you would normally have.
ex: I can't do without my phone.
我沒有手機不行。

en: To leave a place quickly, often to escape.
ex: The thief ran off down the street.
小偷沿著街道逃跑了。

en: To be a disadvantage to someone or something.
ex: His lack of experience told against him.
他缺乏經驗對他不利。

en: Used to show that something is said, written or known by someone or something.
ex: As the saying goes, practice makes perfect.
俗話說熟能生巧。

en: To have an effect on something or to change a situation.
ex: Your help made a big difference.
你的幫助起了很大的作用。

en: To move backward away from someone or something, often because of fear.
ex: She backed away from the barking dog.
她從吠叫的狗身邊後退。

en: To leave school, a competition or a group before completing it.
ex: He dropped out of college to start a business.
他輟學去創業。

en: To give something, such as homework or a report, to a person in authority.
ex: Please hand in your essays by Monday.
請在週一前交論文。

en: To have a very good opinion of someone or something.
ex: Everyone thinks highly of our new teacher.
大家對新老師評價很高。

en: To try as hard as you can to do something.
ex: I did my best to finish the project on time.
我盡力準時完成專案。

en: To stay calm in a difficult or dangerous situation.
col: keep one's head in a crisis
ex: She kept her head and called for help.
她保持冷靜並打電話求救。

en: To continue doing something or happening; or to happen.
ex: The show must go on.
表演必須繼續。

en: To continue to happen or develop; or to accompany someone.
ex: The project is going along nicely.
專案進行得很順利。

en: To stay informed about someone or something so you know where they are or what is happening.
ex: It's hard to keep track of all my appointments.
要掌握我所有的行程很難。

en: To remain loyal to a belief, promise or decision.
ex: She stood to her promise despite the difficulties.
儘管困難，她仍遵守諾言。

en: To become extremely angry suddenly.
ex: Dad blew his top when he saw the mess.
爸爸看到一團亂時大發雷霆。

en: To consider or think of someone or something in a particular way; or to watch without taking part.
ex: They looked on him as a hero.
他們把他視為英雄。

en: To be easy to see or notice; or to be much better than others.
ex: Her red hat made her stand out in the crowd.
她的紅帽子讓她在人群中十分顯眼。

en: To say publicly that you do not agree with or support something.
ex: Many people came out against the new tax.
許多人公開反對新稅。

en: To remember something and consider it when making decisions.
ex: Please keep in mind that the shop closes at six.
請記住商店六點關門。

en: To gain control of something; or to start doing a job from someone else.
ex: She took over as manager last month.
她上個月接任了經理一職。

en: To meet with a problem or difficulty that you have to deal with.
ex: We came up against some unexpected problems.
我們遭遇了一些意料之外的問題。

en: To lift something up; or to delay someone or something; or to support something.
ex: The train was held up by a signal failure.
火車因號誌故障而延誤。

en: To begin doing something, especially in a determined way.
ex: He set about cleaning the garage.
他開始打掃車庫。

en: To look good with something else; or to be part of or to accompany something.
ex: Red wine goes well with steak.
紅酒很適合搭配牛排。

en: To give control or responsibility of something to someone else.
ex: He gave the business over to his daughter.
他把生意交給了女兒。

en: To behave in a way that others should copy.
col: set a good example for children
ex: Parents should set a good example for their kids.
父母應該為孩子樹立好榜樣。

en: To have a friendly relationship with someone.
ph: get on like a house on fire
ex: I get on well with my neighbors.
我和鄰居相處融洽。

en: A situation in which people are willing to accept less than they want in order to agree.
ph: a bit of give and take
col: give and take in a marriage
ex: Every relationship needs some give and take.
每段關係都需要一些互相讓步。

en: To show something proudly so that other people will admire it.
ex: He likes to show off his new car.
他喜歡炫耀他的新車。

en: To break a rule or law; or to be opposite to a wish, belief or expectation.
ex: This decision goes against everything we believe.
這個決定違背了我們所有的信念。

en: To remove something by picking it; or to shoot someone one at a time from a distance.
ex: She picked off the dead leaves from the plant.
她摘掉植物上的枯葉。

en: To go into a place quietly so that no one notices; or to move into a different state.
ex: She slipped into the meeting late and sat at the back.
她遲到後悄悄溜進會議室，坐在後排。

en: To become separated from something it was attached to; or to be successful.
ex: The handle came off in my hand.
把手在我手裡掉了下來。

en: To keep criticizing or treating someone unfairly.
ex: The older boys always pick on the little ones.
大男孩總是欺負小的。

en: To say that you want someone to give you something or to do something.
ex: She asked for a glass of water.
她要了一杯水。

en: To drop to the ground from a standing position; or to collapse.
ex: He slipped on the ice and fell down.
他在冰上滑倒了。

en: To return something to the place where it was before.
ex: Please put the books back on the shelf.
請把書放回書架上。

en: To formally leave a job or position.
ex: The minister resigned from his post after the scandal.
部長在醜聞後辭去了職務。
